standard.title: Planning and Design of River Embankments (Levees) — Guidelines (नदी तटबंध के नियोजन तथा डिजाईन के मार्गदर्शी सिद्धांत) (Second Revision)
standard.sector: Water Resources / Flood and Erosion Management

sectional_committee.name: Flood Management, Erosion Management and Diversion Works Sectional Committee

standard.description: This standard covers the planning and design of river embankments (levees) constructed on dry land to protect agricultural and urban areas from flooding.
standard.scope: This standard covers the planning and design of river embankments (levees) constructed on dry land to protect agricultural and urban areas from flooding.

amendments.summary: No active amendments have been issued on this standard (NIL on this copy).

certification.description: Voluntary Code of Practice. Since IS 12094:2018 is an engineering guideline for civil works, it does not carry an individual mandatory BIS 'ISI Mark' product stamp. However, compliance with its dimensional parameters (such as top width, freeboard, slopes, turning platforms) and analytical requirements (such as backwater analysis and HGL cover) is strictly mandated in public works department (PWD) tenders, irrigation department contracts, and flood-control project approvals by state and central agencies (including the Central Water Commission) to ensure structural safety against catastrophic breaches.
requirements: Requires determining the design HFL utilizing short-term or long-term sub-zone plans from the CWC Directorate of Hydrology, or by referencing the Rashtriya Barh Ayog Report (1980).

In the case of embankments constructed on both sides of a river, the rise in water level due to jacketing must be kept in view. A backwater analysis must be carried out to determine the afflux due to the loss in flood storage after construction.
For homogeneous embankments, a standard top width of 5.0 m to 5.5 m must be provided to accommodate maintenance and service vehicle operations.
Requires providing a structural freeboard of 1.5 m or 1.8 m above the design HFL to prevent overtopping by wave action or hydraulic surges.
Side slopes on both the river side and country side must not be steeper than 1:2 or 1:3. Slopes must be protected with turf (vegetative grass cover) to prevent erosion.

The HGL through the levee is assumed at a slope of 1:4, 1:5, or 1:6. To prevent piping and seepage failures, the countryside slope must cover the HGL by a minimum of 0.6 m of compacted soil. A 1.5 m wide berm (or wider) must be provided on the country side if required to encapsulate the HGL.
Before placing embankment soil, the base seat must be stripped of organic topsoil, roots, and loose material to an average depth of 0.3 m.
A turning platform of 3 m width and 15 m to 30 m in length must be provided at every kilometre along the levee top to facilitate safe turning and passage of maintenance vehicles.
To provide communication from one side of the embankment to the other, ramps at suitable places must be provided as per requirement to prevent subsequent unauthorized cutting of the levee slope.
Embankment design and compaction must prevent common breach modes: overtopping by floods higher than design limits, and improper soil compaction/settlement.
